title: Indifferent things; abuse; magistrate and Mosaic forensics
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Christians stand as not bound by Moses' forensic laws as particular right; what stands as moral in them remains. Carlstadt and Müntzer stand as rejected for binding ye Christian magistrate toward Moses' particular forensic laws. — In indifferent things liberty does not extend toward scandalizing ye weak nor toward fastening a worship belonging toward necessity on adiaphora. Those err most gravely who attach necessary worship toward indifferent things, or pretend things stand as indifferent that stand as not.
pass_b_english: In indifferent things liberty does not extend to scandalizing the weak nor to fastening a worship of necessity on adiaphora. Those err most gravely who attach necessary worship to indifferent things, or pretend things are indifferent that are not.

Christians are not bound by Moses' forensic laws as particular right; what is moral in them remains. Carlstadt and Müntzer are rejected for binding the Christian magistrate to Moses' particular forensic laws.
source_text: In rebus indifferentibus libertas non extenditur ad scandalum infirmorum nec ad necessitatis cultum rebus adiaphoris affingendum. Gravissime peccant qui rebus indifferentibus necessitatis cultum affingunt, vel res adiaphoras esse fingunt quae minime sunt. Christiani non obligantur legibus forensibus Mosis quatenus ius singulare; quod morale in iis manet. Improbandi Carlostadius et Monetarius qui magistratum Christianum necessitati legum particularium forensium Mosis alligarunt (contra Lutherum, Melanchthonem, Calvinum).
